newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt confident of U.S. meat approval.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt confident of U.S. meat approval.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it was confident the United States would approve Canberra's proposed trial of a new meat inspection system.
Washington's backing would boost Australia's export competitiveness, Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson told reporters before leaving for the United States.
Australia wants U.S. approval for its plan to replace government inspection with company-based high tech meat inspections.
The new system would dramatically reduce inspection costs for meat processors.
"It further boosts our export competitiveness and that's what we desperately need for our red meat producers in this country," Anderson said.

"I believe that once again ... we're at the cutting edge of where modern food, science and technology is going," said Anderson, who is also deputy leader of the rural-based National Party, the junior member of the ruling coalition.
"And that's why I've no doubt, that whilst it's taken perhaps a little longer already than we would have liked, we will win with this," he said.
He is due to meet U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and other key government members before leaving the U.S. on Thursday.
He has said that he would also discuss U.S. export subsidies and the impact of the European Union exports of wheat gluten, agricultural policy and climate change.
